facts.text: The strongest case that the sources are sufficient is that they are primary filings, audited for annual periods, internally consistent and recent, so covenant levels and later events would refine a snapshot rather than overturn it. The strongest case that they are not is the debt structure: the parent's debt ranks behind subsidiary liabilities, part of the debt is secured, and guarantees come from named subsidiaries, so consolidated statements cannot show claim priority. facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Amkor's leverage is low but rising fast: net debt reached USD 864.22 million, or 0.61x last-twelve-month EBITDA, after nine months of spending outran operating cash flow, so credit quality now depends on customer advances and delivery of the Arizona build rather than on coverage. Cash interest cover was 15.07x in FY2025, but the latest cash cover is not calculable because nine-month cash interest is not stated. Pro forma for the land purchase expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, net debt is USD 897.22 million and net leverage 0.64x. The USD 1,000 million revolver is undrawn and USD 1.9 billion of customer advances are expected within twelve months. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Net leverage was 0.03x at the end of FY2024 and 0.06x at the end of FY2025 and is 0.61x on last-twelve-month EBITDA of about USD 1.41 billion at September 30, 2026, while gross leverage moved from 1.12x to 1.30x to 1.75x. Net debt rose by about USD 797.32 million in nine months because total debt rose by about USD 1.02 billion, mainly the USD 1,150 million convertible notes issued in May 2026, while cash rose by only about USD 224.67 million. The cause is capital spending: payments for property, plant and equipment were about USD 1.24 billion against operating cash flow of about USD 868.35 million, a shortfall of about USD 368.46 million before about USD 62.10 million of dividends and about USD 32.33 million of share repurchases. Amkor expects about USD 2.5 billion of capital spending in 2026 and has spent USD 553.3 million on the Arizona facility so far, which leaves about USD 1.26 billion to spend in the fourth quarter, so net debt is likely to rise further unless customer advances arrive on schedule. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash interest cover fell from 17.14x in FY2024 to 15.07x in FY2025 because cash interest paid grew 22.13% while EBITDA grew 7.38%. Nine-month cash interest is not stated, so cash cover at September 30, 2026 is not calculable; on accrued interest expense of about USD 73.19 million over the last twelve months, EBITDA cover is 19.30x, a proxy that is not a cash measure. Interest expense for the nine months was about USD 52.60 million against USD 54.85 million a year earlier despite more debt, because the convertible notes carry a 0.00% coupon and part of the interest on the Arizona build is capitalised. The implication is a light interest burden today; the USD 1,150 million principal falls due after 2030, so the cost shows up as refinancing or conversion risk, not as coverage. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20; calculation C05; calculation C07

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Operating cash flow for nine months grew 92.48% to about USD 868.35 million, which Amkor attributes to higher operating profit, customer advance payments and working capital changes. Contract liabilities rose from USD 390.8 million at year-end 2025 to USD 547.6 million, so customer advances are now a material non-debt source of funds for the Arizona build: they must be earned by delivering product, are backed by USD 200.0 million of standby letters of credit and are not in the debt figures. Operating cash flow less capital spending was a shortfall of about USD 156.06 million over the last twelve months. The mechanism is that capital spending is paid first while advances arrive later, so a slowdown in advances while spending continues would fall on cash and the revolver. facts.text: Amkor states no EBITDA, so EBITDA here is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization; adding other income, mainly interest, would raise last-twelve-month EBITDA by 5.25% and lower gross leverage to 1.66x. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case that credit quality is stable is that net leverage is still 0.61x, cash and short-term investments of USD 2,376.2 million are close to total debt, the revolver is undrawn and Amkor expects USD 1.9 billion of customer advances within twelve months and USD 1.3 billion in 2027; if those advances arrive, net debt could stop rising. The case against is that about USD 2.5 billion of capital spending and USD 2,635.3 million of purchase obligations are committed while the advances are expected, not received, and cash interest cover cannot yet be measured on the latest twelve months. Quarterly capital spending, the contract liabilities balance, any revolver draw and the first cash interest figure for the nine months are the observable tests: a falling contract liabilities balance or a drawn revolver would worsen the view, while receipt of the 2027 advance with spending falling back would improve it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–37; calculation C06; calculation C14

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Amkor is a scaled but concentrated contract manufacturer under family influence, so creditors depend on one dominant customer relationship and on payout and capital spending choices made while the Arizona build absorbs cash. One customer, Apple, supplied 29.8% of FY2025 net sales and the ten largest customers 72%. The Kim family and affiliates hold about 49.5% of the shares, and the part of that stake above an aggregate 41.6% of voting shares is voted neutrally under an agreement. Governance risk reads Medium rather than Low because dividends of USD 62.1 million and buybacks of USD 32.3 million continued while capital spending is funded with debt, but the sources document no related-party leakage, extraction or restructuring. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Customer concentration is the largest business risk. Apple accounted for 29.8% and Qualcomm for 11.1% of FY2025 net sales and the ten largest customers for 72%. In the three months to September 30, 2026 the communications end market fell from 51% to 37% of net sales, down 28%, because of the timing of transferring system-in-package programs from Korea to Vietnam, while the computing and the automotive and industrial end markets each grew 37%. Factory loading follows a few customers' program timing, so a program transfer or a lost design moves utilization and margin quickly. The implication is volatile quarterly earnings around a growing base: gross margin of 18.3% against 14.3% a year earlier came from a mix with lower material content and may not persist. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Capital intensity is rising and the payback is distant. Amkor expects about USD 2.5 billion of capital spending in 2026, mainly to build the Arizona facility, whose first phase is not expected to start manufacturing until the first half of 2028. Government support is conditional: a direct funding award of up to USD 407 million had produced no cash by September 30, 2026 and carries milestones and clawback rights, and the investment tax credit rate rose from 25% to 35% for property placed in service after 2025. Cash is committed years before revenue, so creditors should expect a long stretch of spending funded by debt and customer advances until the facility ramps. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Control sits with the Kim family, which holds about 49.5% of the shares and, through the Chairman, can substantially influence shareholder and board decisions. A voting agreement requires the part of the stake above an aggregate 41.6% of voting shares to be voted neutrally, which limits control of that part but not of the rest. For creditors the mechanism is that a recapitalisation or takeover needs family consent and the family's incentives are tied to the franchise; the sources show a regular dividend, not special distributions, so no extraction is documented. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 76

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Financial policy has been to refinance and fund growth with new debt while keeping a regular dividend. In 2025 the 2027 senior notes were redeemed with the proceeds of USD 500.0 million of 2033 senior notes and a term loan under a USD 1.0 billion secured revolving facility, and in May 2026 Amkor issued USD 1.15 billion of convertible notes with a capped call that cost USD 56.4 million. Payouts of USD 62.1 million in dividends over nine months and USD 32.3 million of repurchases in the third quarter under a USD 300.0 million authorization are small beside capital spending, but they continue while debt funds the build, which is why governance risk is Medium. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better governance view is that family ownership aligns long-term incentives with a capital-intensive franchise, payouts are small beside capital spending, and no related-party leakage, restructuring or creditor-adverse transaction appears in the sources read, while customers are prepaying about USD 1.9 billion for capacity. The view would worsen on a debt-funded special distribution, related-party dealings disclosed in the proxy statement, a revolver draw to fund payouts, or loss of the largest customer's programs; it would improve if the proxy statement shows a majority of independent directors and no related-party payments and the debt documents show tight restricted-payment limits. facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Amkor is a low-leverage, liquid credit entering a heavily debt-funded capacity build, so creditors are exposed to execution and customer-funding risk rather than to coverage or near-term maturities. Net leverage rose from 0.06x at the end of 2025 to 0.61x at September 30, 2026, or 0.64x pro forma for the Arizona land purchase expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, largely because nine-month capital spending of USD 1.24 billion exceeded operating cash flow of USD 868.35 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K01; calculation K03

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Debt service is not the constraint; the investment program is. Last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 1.41 billion covers accrued interest expense 19.30x, and in the first nine months of 2026 interest income of USD 59.12 million exceeded interest expense of USD 52.60 million, helped by the 0.00% coupon on the largest new issue, the convertible notes due 2031, and by interest capitalized on the Arizona build. Cash interest cover was 15.07x in FY2025 and cash interest for 2026 is not printed. The implication is that the debt stack could absorb a materially weaker earnings year before coverage became the issue, so the credit question is whether cash generation keeps pace with spending. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The earnings base behind the build is improving but narrow. Third-quarter net sales were flat at USD 1,990.56 million, up 0.18%, while gross margin widened to 18.3% from 14.3% because materials cost fell USD 132.87 million on a lower-material-content mix, and conversion costs of labor, depreciation and other manufacturing rose USD 57.42 million, or 10.25%. Communications sales fell 28% on the timing of system-in-package transfers from Korea to Vietnam while computing and automotive and industrial each grew 37%. One customer was 29.8% and a second 11.1% of FY2025 net sales, the ten largest customers were 72%, and the filings give no contract terms. The margin gain is mix rather than price, and a few customers' program timing can move factory loading and earnings quickly. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity and the maturity ladder are not the near-term risk. Cash and short-term investments of USD 2,376.2 million plus the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver, which expires in May 2030, give USD 3,376.2 million against stated twelve-month obligations of USD 2,926.5 million, or 1.15x before operating cash flow and customer advances, although 57.09% of the cash and investments is held offshore and is reachable mainly by repaying intercompany debt. Only USD 348.89 million of principal falls due in 2027 to 2029 and 66.11% falls due after 2030, entirely the 2031 convertible and 2033 senior notes. Level 1 quotes put the 2033 senior notes at 94.77% of principal and the convertible at 90.71%, below par but not at distressed levels. The conversion price of the convertible is 2.23x the average price of the latest share repurchases and principal is settled in cash, so it is best read as cash debt due in 2031. Pro forma cash for the land purchase and the customer agreement is not established. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Financial policy is the main governance variable and is now being tested. Payouts of USD 94.43 million in nine months, made up of dividends of USD 62.10 million and repurchases of USD 32.33 million, continued while free cash flow was negative, and management states it aims to return 40% to 50% of cumulative free cash flow generated since 2022. Cumulative payouts are 45.08% of cumulative issuer-defined free cash flow, but a fourth-quarter free cash outflow above USD 105.71 million would lift that above 50% at current payouts, so either payouts slow, which supports creditors, or the framework is stretched. The Kim family holds 49.5% of the shares, so a sale or takeover is unlikely without family support and payout decisions rest with a family-influenced board; no related-party leakage is documented, but the proxy statement is not supplied and covenant levels are not printed, so room under the dividend restriction is not tested. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Claims are layered in a way the consolidated figures do not show. Debt of USD 845.8 million is collateralized, an amount equal to the Term A Loans plus the Korean and Japanese subsidiary loans although the filing does not say which loans carry the collateral, the 2031 and 2033 notes are senior unsecured, and the parent's debt is structurally subordinated to all subsidiary liabilities. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a weakening view is that Amkor starts the build from low net leverage of 0.61x, or 0.64x pro forma for the expected land purchase, with net interest income, USD 3,376.2 million of cash, short-term investments and undrawn revolver, little principal due before 2030 and customers who are prepaying for capacity, which suggests the demand is contracted rather than hoped for. Capital spending that is not yet contracted can be deferred, and EBITDA margin moved up to 20.66% in the third quarter from 16.23% a year earlier. The case that the credit is weaker than that is that reported cash flow already leans on advances, commitments nearly doubled in one quarter, third-quarter sales barely grew, the largest customer is 29.8% of sales and covenants cannot be tested. The view would improve if advances arrive on schedule while 2027 spending is held back, if the USD 407 million government award starts to be received, or if quarterly free cash flow turns positive. It would worsen if advances slip, the revolver is drawn to fund spending, a major customer's programs are lost, the mix-driven margin gain reverses, or payouts continue after cumulative free cash flow falls below the level that supports them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–37; calculation K01; calculation K14; calculation K21; calculation K22

facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Amkor is the largest US-headquartered outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider. It packages and tests chips designed by integrated device makers, fabless companies and foundries, usually on silicon wafers that the customer consigns, and reports one operating segment. The business model supports cash-flow visibility only in part: the filings describe short customer commitments and no backlog, so there is little contractual protection, but consigned wafers and customer responsibility for unused materials limit the inventory risk Amkor carries, and the move of sales toward computing and automotive reduces dependence on smartphones. The table that follows shows the mix and why it matters: the shift is real in the latest quarter, but one quarter's mix is also moved by the timing of program transfers. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Amkor is a listed company whose votes are substantially influenced by one family. Susan Y. Kim, the Chairman, and family members and affiliates own about 49.5% of the shares and can determine or substantially influence shareholder votes and board elections; about 29.6 million of those shares, received in a 2013 note exchange, are subject to a voting agreement that requires them to be voted neutrally to the extent the family's aggregate voting holding exceeds 41.6%. For creditors the mechanism is that a leveraged recapitalization or sale needs family support and family interests are tied to the franchise, which lowers takeover risk, while payout policy is set by a family-influenced board. The parent borrows and issues the notes; the Korean and Japanese subsidiaries borrow locally, Guardian Assets, Inc. guarantees the notes and the revolver, and Amkor Technology Singapore Holding Pte. Ltd. also guarantees the revolver, so debt of the parent is structurally behind subsidiary liabilities. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 74–75; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is cyclical, concentrated and exposed to program timing, not recurring. FY2025 net sales were USD 6,707.981 million, with 29.8% from the largest customer, 11.1% from a second and 72% from the ten largest; communications fell as a share from 46% in FY2025 to 37% in the third quarter of 2026. Management describes the semiconductor industry as cyclical and lists the absence of backlog and the short-term nature of customer commitments among the factors that move results, so volume visibility beyond the advance payment agreements is limited. Pricing power is not evidenced: the gross margin gain came from a lower-material-content mix and higher utilization, not from stated price increases. The credit consequence is that a program transfer, lost design or inventory correction at one or two customers moves revenue and utilization faster than costs can adjust, while growth in computing and in automotive and industrial of 37% each in the third quarter shows where new volume is coming from. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 30–31, 50

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins can be defended in a growth quarter but not shown to hold under volume pressure. Materials were 50.7% of third-quarter net sales against 57.5% a year earlier, and because customers consign wafers and bear unused materials, materials behave largely as a pass-through, so the margin is set by what remains after materials. Net sales less materials rose 16.15% to USD 981.264 million while conversion costs rose 10.25%, which is operating leverage working in Amkor's favor; with a substantial fixed cost base, the same leverage reverses when volume falls. Labor was 10.1% of net sales and depreciation 8.6%, and depreciation will rise as the Arizona facility is placed in service. The implication is that EBITDA margin of 20.66% in the third quarter should be read as a favorable-mix level until a falling-volume quarter shows the floor. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 29–31; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation K13; calculation K14

facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Cash conversion has turned from supportive to dependent on advances. Issuer-defined free cash flow was USD 359.275 million in FY2024 and USD 307.873 million in FY2025 and was negative USD 319.068 million in the first nine months of 2026; on the stricter measure of operating cash flow less capital spending the third quarter alone was negative USD 61.609 million against negative USD 306.852 million in the first half. facts.label: Covenants, liquidity detail and claims outside debt
facts.text: The agreements governing the debt contain a minimum interest coverage ratio and a maximum consolidated leverage ratio, and management states that Amkor was in compliance at September 30, 2026 and expects to remain so for at least twelve months; no level, step-down or definition is printed, so headroom is not calculable and the leverage computed here, carrying debt over calculated EBITDA, may differ from the covenant definition. Liquidity at that date was cash and cash equivalents of USD 1,603.015 million, short-term investments of USD 773.181 million, the undrawn revolver of USD 1,000.0 million expiring in May 2030 and USD 62.1 million available under subsidiary facilities, of which the Korean facility of about USD 59 million expires in May 2027, within twelve months. USD 200.0 million of standby letters of credit are outstanding against customer advances; the filing states the full revolver as available, so they do not appear to reduce it, but the issuing facility is not stated. Claims outside the debt figure are finance lease obligations of USD 185.6 million and operating lease obligations of USD 98.5 million in future minimum payments, pension and severance obligations of USD 73.931 million, purchase obligations of USD 2,687.6 million and non-recourse receivable factoring of USD 30.4 million in nine months; management expects no material effect from legal proceedings, and none of these items is added to debt here. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is moderated by technical barriers at the advanced end, where flip chip, memory and wafer-level processing were 81.82% of nine-month sales, but the annual report names established providers mainly in Asia, contract foundries and electronics manufacturers offering some advanced packaging, Chinese firms building a China-for-China supply chain and customers' own in-house capabilities; mainstream wirebond products, 18.18% of sales, are where that rivalry is least cushioned by technology. New entrants face high capital needs, which is also the burden Amkor carries. Substitutes are in-house packaging by foundries and integrated device makers, which would remove volume rather than price. Buyer power is the dominant force: the ten largest customers were 72% of net sales and the largest alone 29.8%, and commitments are short, so a large customer can move programs between suppliers and sites, as the transfer from Korea to Vietnam shows; credit consequence is volatile utilization and a margin that depends on retaining a few programs. Supplier power over laminate substrates, leadframes and wire is partly neutralized because customers bear unused materials. facts.label: PEST analysis
facts.text: Policy and trade conditions are material to credit quality here, so the analysis is run. Political and regulatory factors cut both ways: the USD 407 million government award and a 35% investment tax credit support the Arizona build but are conditional, and trade restrictions, tariffs and the tension around Korea and Taiwan threaten a supply chain with 54.20% of net property, plant and equipment in Korea. Economic factors are cyclical demand and currency: the 37% growth in computing and in automotive and industrial rests on data-center and driver-assistance spending, which is cyclical, and Amkor has hedged part of its net investment in foreign subsidiaries. Technological change favors Amkor while it keeps pace in advanced packaging, which is why capital spending is rising. The credit implication is that policy support is real but conditional, and geographic concentration in Korea raises the severity of a regional disruption. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 41, 50, 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 62, 129; calculation K16

facts.label: SWOT analysis
facts.text: Strengths: the scale and technology position in advanced packaging, low net leverage of 0.61x, 0.64x pro forma for the expected land purchase, a ladder with little due before 2030, and customers prepaying for capacity. Weaknesses: capital spending that exceeds operating cash flow, customer concentration, thin free cash flow and operating cash flow that leans on advances, and unprinted covenant levels. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: receipt of the government award and of the advances, a ramp of the Arizona facility that diversifies production geography, and growth in computing and automotive end markets. Threats that could weaken it: a loss or transfer of programs at the largest customers, a cyclical downturn while commitments are signed, trade policy and regional conflict affecting Korea, and shareholder payouts that outrun free cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–37, 50; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K01; calculation K16

facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position are the clearest support: net sales of USD 7,461.269 million over the last twelve months and the position as the largest US-headquartered provider make the issuer large enough to absorb shocks. Competitive advantage rests on advanced packaging capability that customers are paying to reserve, though no contract terms are disclosed. Business diversification is mixed: end markets are spread, but customers and the Korean asset base are concentrated. Cost and capex flexibility is narrow while USD 1,951 million of construction is contracted. Margin stability is the weaker side of the earnings profile because the latest gain is mix-driven. Free cash flow stability is the weakest dimension, negative on both definitions in 2026 and flattered by advances. Refinancing and capital markets access is shown by USD 1.15 billion of convertible notes in May 2026 and USD 500.0 million of notes in September 2025, though quotes are below par. Liquidity is adequate with cash, short-term investments and the revolver exceeding stated twelve-month obligations 1.15x. Financial policy and governance is moderate: family control, continuing payouts and unprinted covenants offset the absence of documented extraction. On the broader definition that also deducts short-term investments, net debt at September 30, 2026 was USD 91.04 million against net cash of USD 546.14 million at the end of 2025, and a pro forma figure for the land purchase is not established. The trend is a strong balance sheet drifting toward heavier use of it, with key missing data in covenant terms and customer contracts. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is for rising capital spending and rising net debt, with timing set by advance receipts. Tailwinds are demand for advanced packaging in computing and automotive, customer prepayments, the ramp of the Vietnam facility, the investment tax credit and the Korean grant support of up to about USD 110 million; headwinds are the doubling of commitments, higher depreciation from new capacity, program transfers, and the cyclical risk that customers' demand falls after capacity is built. Over three to five years the first phase of the Arizona facility is expected to start manufacturing in the first half of 2028, so the payoff arrives after the spending peak and the credit depends on utilization then. Sector headwinds are tariffs, export controls and regional tension; company-specific headwinds are customer concentration and the family-influenced payout policy. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside is a delay in customer advances or a pause in a lead customer's programs while the contracted spending continues. The first operational break would be falling utilization at plants that have a substantial fixed cost base, which turns a flat sales quarter into lower gross margin because conversion costs rose USD 57.42 million year on year. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA and operating cash flow, with the advance build ceasing to add cash; the shortfall falls first on cash and short-term investments of USD 2,376.2 million and then on the USD 1,000 million revolver. As an illustration only, if the fourth quarter repeats the third quarter's operating cash flow while capital spending reaches the USD 1.26 billion implied by guidance, the fourth-quarter free cash outflow would be USD 776.42 million, 32.67% of cash and short-term investments, and if last-twelve-month EBITDA were also 25% lower, net leverage would be about 1.55x. That would not threaten liquidity within twelve months, but a revolver draw would increase secured claims ahead of the unsecured notes and would test covenant levels that are not printed. The observable triggers are slipping advance receipts, quarterly free cash outflow above the third quarter's USD 61.609 million, a revolver draw, and sales below the year-earlier quarter. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress over the next twelve months on the stated liquidity; the weak point is any later period in which advances do not arrive while spending stays at contracted levels, because 2027 spending and customer terms are not stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 25, 30, 34–37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amkr_amkr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation K03; calculation K05; calculation K06; calculation K13

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Amkor presents an adequate but concentrated business profile supported by scale, advanced packaging capability, low leverage and prepaying customers, but credit quality is constrained by a debt-funded capacity build, customer concentration and unprinted covenant levels. Cash-flow durability appears adequate and dependent on advances: EBITDA covers interest comfortably, yet free cash flow is negative on both definitions in 2026. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivering the Arizona facility on time and on keeping the revolver and Term A Loans, both due in May 2030, available through the build. The primary downside path is a slip in advance receipts or a loss of lead customer programs while spending of USD 1,951 million is contracted. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, customer advance terms, a total cost for the Arizona facility, ratings and peer figures. Fundamental credit synthesis completed. Top risk: customer-funded capacity spending that is committed before the cash arrives. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 34–37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K01; calculation K03; calculation K11

spans.text: ## Request

Source readiness for Amkor Technology, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is whether the five supplied filings can support the requested financial foundation, business and governance and fundamental credit work, and what remains missing.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_amkr_amkr-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-21 | 8304a687dbd52f3a21878d9b5221a89e472cd66516ae6da68b919b9d4bf1cbf9 | Audited FY2024, FY2023 and FY2022 income statements and December 31, 2024 and 2023 balance sheets as first published; checked against the later annual report; the date is the signature page date. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-20 | 67a9e9bb291e8e2836040251ea08bc811c3bf50f3e6a0caca1636af522edb78a | Audited FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 statements, business, risk factor, debt, liquidity and ownership disclosures, exhibit list and Part III incorporation by reference; the date is the signature page date. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_amkr_amkr-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-28 | 11adb20adcf00937bb63ea8d0d6539b2ef424bda202e21cab1814b97e27b9ae6 | Unaudited three-month statements to March 31, 2026 with 2025 comparatives, debt and liquidity at that date; the date is the signature page date. |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_amkr_amkr-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-28 | e5511d8d392092faff271ab7db1fba7436c904a1296c1e84451e1221951ad3eb | Unaudited three- and six-month statements to June 30, 2026 with 2025 comparatives, debt and liquidity at that date; the date is the signature page date. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-27 | 71c4688f61c8c8b537e875298c930c20e3abc00b6f57c61b7762a2695e5d6db0 | Latest source: unaudited three- and nine-month statements, September 30, 2026 balance sheet, debt note, liquidity and covenant wording, October 2026 customer agreement; the date is the signature page date. |
No analysis from another module was supplied to this module or used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied Amkor filings are sufficient for the requested credit snapshot through the quarter ended September 30, 2026, but creditors should treat covenant levels, executed debt terms and anything after October 27, 2026 as unverified. The FY2024 and FY2025 annual statements carry audit opinions and the 2026 quarterly statements are unaudited. Where filings overlap they agree: FY2024 results match across both annual reports and reported debt of USD 2,467.2 million ties between the balance sheet and the debt note. The FY2025 and 2026 filings name a minimum interest coverage test and a maximum leverage test but print no level, and the latest filing was signed 22 days before the as-of date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C7
### Key findings

The sources cover the registrant, Amkor Technology, Inc., on a consolidated basis with its subsidiaries: two annual reports and the first, second and third quarter 2026 reports. Together they give income statements for four fiscal years, balance sheets at each December 31 from 2023 to 2025 and at each 2026 quarter end, and cash flow statements, so the requested work can be sourced from primary filings. The filings name Amkor Technology Singapore Holding Pte. Ltd. and Guardian Assets, Inc. as guarantors of certain debt, and no separate issuer or parent perimeter applies.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_amkr_amkr-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 86–89; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–93; 10-Q_2026-03-31_amkr_amkr-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amkr_amkr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 4–8, 19, 21

The numbers reconcile wherever the filings overlap. FY2024 and FY2023 income statement lines, including net sales and net income attributable to Amkor, are identical in both annual reports, total assets at December 31, 2025 agree between the FY2025 annual report and the latest quarterly report, cash including restricted cash ties to the cash flow statement at both dates, and debt on the balance sheet ties to the debt note and to the liquidity discussion. No restatement of earlier statements was found in any of the five files.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-K_2024-12-31_amkr_amkr-20241231.htm.jsonl; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl; 10-Q_2026-03-31_amkr_amkr-20260331.htm.jsonl; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amkr_amkr-20260630.htm.jsonl; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl

The debt note lists senior notes due 2033, convertible senior notes due 2031, a senior secured revolving facility with USD 1.0 billion available, term loans and subsidiary loans, and states that USD 845.8 million of debt is collateralized. The parent's debt is structurally subordinated to subsidiary liabilities, so consolidated statements alone do not show which claims sit where. The FY2025 annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports name a minimum interest coverage ratio and a maximum consolidated leverage ratio but print no required level, and the executed credit agreement, its amendment and both indentures are not supplied, so headroom against covenants is not established.

The latest filing was signed on October 27, 2026, 22 days before the as-of date, and no earnings release or current report is supplied for the period after it. That filing itself discloses an October 2026 customer advance payment agreement under which about USD 1.3 billion is expected in 2027. Any other event between October 27 and November 18, 2026 is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 84; calculation C1

Directors, executive officers, compensation and the beneficial ownership table are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied, so board and management detail is limited to what the filings state elsewhere. The risk factors state that Susan Y. Kim and members of her family and affiliates owned about 49.5% of the common stock at September 30, 2026, which makes ownership concentration a governance fact the filings do establish.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 131–133; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75

The run settings supply no ratings, quotes, peer set, portfolio or legal documents, and the filings give no issuer credit rating, so ratings, market-implied and relative-value inputs are not established from this source set.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 50, 70
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that the sources are sufficient is that they are primary filings, audited for annual periods, internally consistent and recent, so covenant levels and later events would refine a snapshot rather than overturn it. The strongest case that they are not is the debt structure: the parent's debt ranks behind subsidiary liabilities, part of the debt is secured, and guarantees come from named subsidiaries, so consolidated statements cannot show claim priority. The executed credit agreement, its amendment and both indentures would let covenant levels, guarantors and collateral be read from executed terms, and a filing dated after October 27, 2026 would show whether the October 2026 customer agreement or any new financing has changed the picture.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 35–36
### Limitations
Covenant levels, executed debt terms and security detail beyond the notes to the statements are not established from the supplied files.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 136

Events between October 27, 2026 and the as-of date are not established, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is not published as a stand-alone quarter, so it and any trailing measure must be derived by differencing the annual and year-to-date statements.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–8, 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–93
Readiness here concerns source sufficiency only; it makes no credit, legal or investment conclusion.

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for Amkor Technology, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the consolidated statements for FY2024, FY2025 and the three and nine months to September 30, 2026, with carrying-value debt, net debt, leverage, cash interest cover, liquidity and the maturity ladder.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-27 | 71c4688f61c8c8b537e875298c930c20e3abc00b6f57c61b7762a2695e5d6db0 | Unaudited three- and nine-month statements and balance sheet at September 30, 2026; debt, fair value, commitments and liquidity discussion; post-quarter events; the date is the signature page date. |

No external sources were used. Dates above are the signature page dates printed in each filing.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Amkor's leverage is low but rising fast: net debt reached USD 864.22 million, or 0.61x last-twelve-month EBITDA, after nine months of spending outran operating cash flow, so credit quality now depends on customer advances and delivery of the Arizona build rather than on coverage. Gross leverage rose from 1.30x at year-end 2025 to 1.75x and net leverage from 0.06x to 0.61x, because the USD 1,150 million convertible issue funded capital spending that exceeded operating cash flow by about USD 368.46 million. Cash interest cover was 15.07x in FY2025, but the latest cash cover is not calculable because nine-month cash interest is not stated. Pro forma for the land purchase expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, net debt is USD 897.22 million and net leverage 0.64x. The USD 1,000 million revolver is undrawn and USD 1.9 billion of customer advances are expected within twelve months.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C07
### Key findings

Net leverage was 0.03x at the end of FY2024 and 0.06x at the end of FY2025 and is 0.61x on last-twelve-month EBITDA of about USD 1.41 billion at September 30, 2026, while gross leverage moved from 1.12x to 1.30x to 1.75x. Net debt rose by about USD 797.32 million in nine months because total debt rose by about USD 1.02 billion, mainly the USD 1,150 million convertible notes issued in May 2026, while cash rose by only about USD 224.67 million. The cause is capital spending: payments for property, plant and equipment were about USD 1.24 billion against operating cash flow of about USD 868.35 million, a shortfall of about USD 368.46 million before about USD 62.10 million of dividends and about USD 32.33 million of share repurchases. Amkor expects about USD 2.5 billion of capital spending in 2026 and has spent USD 553.3 million on the Arizona facility so far, which leaves about USD 1.26 billion to spend in the fourth quarter, so net debt is likely to rise further unless customer advances arrive on schedule.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06

Cash interest cover fell from 17.14x in FY2024 to 15.07x in FY2025 because cash interest paid grew 22.13% while EBITDA grew 7.38%. Nine-month cash interest is not stated, so cash cover at September 30, 2026 is not calculable; on accrued interest expense of about USD 73.19 million over the last twelve months, EBITDA cover is 19.30x, a proxy that is not a cash measure. Interest expense for the nine months was about USD 52.60 million against USD 54.85 million a year earlier despite more debt, because the convertible notes carry a 0.00% coupon and part of the interest on the Arizona build is capitalised. The implication is a light interest burden today; the USD 1,150 million principal falls due after 2030, so the cost shows up as refinancing or conversion risk, not as coverage.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20; calculation C05; calculation C07

Operating cash flow for nine months grew 92.48% to about USD 868.35 million, which Amkor attributes to higher operating profit, customer advance payments and working capital changes. Contract liabilities rose from USD 390.8 million at year-end 2025 to USD 547.6 million, so customer advances are now a material non-debt source of funds for the Arizona build: they must be earned by delivering product, are backed by USD 200.0 million of standby letters of credit and are not in the debt figures. Operating cash flow less capital spending was a shortfall of about USD 156.06 million over the last twelve months. The mechanism is that capital spending is paid first while advances arrive later, so a slowdown in advances while spending continues would fall on cash and the revolver.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C05; calculation C06

Cash and short-term investments were USD 2,376.2 million, of which USD 1,356.5 million is held by foreign subsidiaries and reachable mainly by repaying intercompany debt, and the USD 1,000 million revolver is undrawn, together USD 3,376.2 million. Stated obligations due within twelve months, namely debt, purchase obligations of USD 2,635.3 million, interest and leases, total USD 2,926.5 million, so liquidity covers them 1.15x before operating cash flow and the USD 1.9 billion of expected customer advances. The maturity ladder is back-ended: 66.11% of contractual principal falls due after 2030, entirely the 2031 convertible and 2033 senior notes, so refinancing risk is distant and the near-term test is funding capital spending, not repaying debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C08; calculation C14

After the balance sheet date Amkor reports an October 2026 agreement with a customer under which it expects USD 1.3 billion in 2027, and an agreement to buy additional Arizona land for about USD 33 million expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. Both are kept out of the period figures: the land purchase is a pro forma adjustment that takes net debt to USD 897.22 million and net leverage to 0.64x, and the customer receipt has not occurred and is not adjusted.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C10

Amkor states no EBITDA, so EBITDA here is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization; adding other income, mainly interest, would raise last-twelve-month EBITDA by 5.25% and lower gross leverage to 1.66x. Net debt deducts only cash and cash equivalents; also deducting short-term investments of about USD 773.18 million would lower it to about USD 91.04 million. Lease obligations of USD 185.6 million for finance leases and USD 98.5 million for operating leases, in undiscounted future payments, sit outside debt. Calculating EBITDA without other income and deducting cash only make leverage look higher than the issuer's own cash presentation would, while keeping leases outside debt makes it look lower.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C03; calculation C05
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that credit quality is stable is that net leverage is still 0.61x, cash and short-term investments of USD 2,376.2 million are close to total debt, the revolver is undrawn and Amkor expects USD 1.9 billion of customer advances within twelve months and USD 1.3 billion in 2027; if those advances arrive, net debt could stop rising. The case against is that about USD 2.5 billion of capital spending and USD 2,635.3 million of purchase obligations are committed while the advances are expected, not received, and cash interest cover cannot yet be measured on the latest twelve months. Quarterly capital spending, the contract liabilities balance, any revolver draw and the first cash interest figure for the nine months are the observable tests: a falling contract liabilities balance or a drawn revolver would worsen the view, while receipt of the 2027 advance with spending falling back would improve it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–37; calculation C06; calculation C14
### Limitations
Amkor states no EBITDA, so every EBITDA-based ratio rests on a figure calculated here, and no issuer-adjusted measure exists to compare it with.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7
Cash interest for the nine-month periods is not stated, so cash interest cover for the latest twelve months is not calculable, and the accrued-basis proxy is not a substitute.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8
Security and ranking of the Korea and Japan term loans are not stated individually, so the debt stack is partial and no recovery inference should be drawn from it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21
The pro forma adjustment is mechanical, applied to the September 30, 2026 position alone, and is not a forecast.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

## Gaps

- Medium: Cash interest paid is not stated for the nine-month periods of 2026 and 2025, so cash interest cover at September 30, 2026 and last-twelve-month cash interest are not calculable; a supplemental interest paid line in the interim statements or an earnings release would close it.

- Medium: The credit agreement and the indentures are not supplied and the filings print no covenant level, so covenant capacity, step-downs and guarantor scope beyond the notes' descriptions are not established; the executed documents would close it.

- Low: Amkor states no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization for every period; the issuer's own definition would close it, and adding other income would change the last twelve months by the amount shown in the definition register.

- Low: The interim cash flow statements are condensed, so the annual lines for deferred taxes, share-based compensation, working capital movements and similar items are not printed for the nine-month columns, and the annual statements do not print the capped call and repurchase lines; those cells are marked not supplied.

- Low: Several cells are printed as dashes in the sources (loss on debt retirement in FY2024, current restricted cash at 2025-12-31, the revolving credit facility lines, short-term debt lines in FY2025, capped calls and repurchases in the first nine months of 2025); they are shown as not supplied, not as zero.

- Low: The Korea and Japan term loans state no individual security or legal rank; the filing gives collateralized debt of USD 845.8 million in aggregate, which equals the sum of the Term A Loans and those loans, so they are left out of the debt stack; the debt agreements would close it.
- Low: The revolving credit facility balance is printed as a dash while availability equals capacity; it is shown as undrawn in the debt stack, but the filing states no drawn amount.

- Low: Carrying values are disclosed only for the two note issues and for all loans together, so each loan is kept at principal and one financing cost adjustment of negative 3.185 reconciles them to Total Debt.

- Low: The customer advance payment expected in 2027 is approximate and unreceived, and the non-current part of customer advances is not separated in the sources read, so no pro forma net debt is stated for it.
- Low: FY2023 and earlier periods and the interim positions at March 31 and June 30, 2026 are in the supplied filings but are not tabulated; a trend before FY2024 is outside this snapshot.

- Low: Cash and short-term investments held offshore are reachable mainly through intercompany debt repayment and may bear withholding or state taxes, so the amount of freely transferable cash is not established.

No conflict between filings was found where periods overlap; the FY2024 income statement and the balance sheet lines compared agree across the two annual reports, and every statement identity holds without a difference.

Business and governance fact pack for Amkor Technology, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the company, its customers and end markets, ownership and control, financing transactions and shareholder payouts, and governance and disclosure, from the supplied filings through September 30, 2026.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Amkor is a scaled but concentrated contract manufacturer under family influence, so creditors depend on one dominant customer relationship and on payout and capital spending choices made while the Arizona build absorbs cash. One customer, Apple, supplied 29.8% of FY2025 net sales and the ten largest customers 72%. The Kim family and affiliates hold about 49.5% of the shares, and the part of that stake above an aggregate 41.6% of voting shares is voted neutrally under an agreement. Governance risk reads Medium rather than Low because dividends of USD 62.1 million and buybacks of USD 32.3 million continued while capital spending is funded with debt, but the sources document no related-party leakage, extraction or restructuring.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 83
### Key findings

Customer concentration is the largest business risk. Apple accounted for 29.8% and Qualcomm for 11.1% of FY2025 net sales and the ten largest customers for 72%. In the three months to September 30, 2026 the communications end market fell from 51% to 37% of net sales, down 28%, because of the timing of transferring system-in-package programs from Korea to Vietnam, while the computing and the automotive and industrial end markets each grew 37%. Factory loading follows a few customers' program timing, so a program transfer or a lost design moves utilization and margin quickly. The implication is volatile quarterly earnings around a growing base: gross margin of 18.3% against 14.3% a year earlier came from a mix with lower material content and may not persist.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

Capital intensity is rising and the payback is distant. Amkor expects about USD 2.5 billion of capital spending in 2026, mainly to build the Arizona facility, whose first phase is not expected to start manufacturing until the first half of 2028. Government support is conditional: a direct funding award of up to USD 407 million had produced no cash by September 30, 2026 and carries milestones and clawback rights, and the investment tax credit rate rose from 25% to 35% for property placed in service after 2025. Cash is committed years before revenue, so creditors should expect a long stretch of spending funded by debt and customer advances until the facility ramps.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75

Control sits with the Kim family, which holds about 49.5% of the shares and, through the Chairman, can substantially influence shareholder and board decisions. A voting agreement requires the part of the stake above an aggregate 41.6% of voting shares to be voted neutrally, which limits control of that part but not of the rest. For creditors the mechanism is that a recapitalisation or takeover needs family consent and the family's incentives are tied to the franchise; the sources show a regular dividend, not special distributions, so no extraction is documented.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 76

Financial policy has been to refinance and fund growth with new debt while keeping a regular dividend. In 2025 the 2027 senior notes were redeemed with the proceeds of USD 500.0 million of 2033 senior notes and a term loan under a USD 1.0 billion secured revolving facility, and in May 2026 Amkor issued USD 1.15 billion of convertible notes with a capped call that cost USD 56.4 million. Payouts of USD 62.1 million in dividends over nine months and USD 32.3 million of repurchases in the third quarter under a USD 300.0 million authorization are small beside capital spending, but they continue while debt funds the build, which is why governance risk is Medium.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 83

Customer advance payments are becoming part of how the build is funded: Amkor expects about USD 1.9 billion within twelve months and, under an October 2026 agreement, about USD 1.3 billion in 2027. This is a non-debt source of funds that must be earned by delivering capacity and is partly backed by standby letters of credit, so it lowers the borrowing need only if customer demand and Amkor's delivery both hold.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete on governance. The annual statements are audited by the same firm since 2000 and the latest quarterly report states effective disclosure controls, but board independence, related-party transactions, compensation and the ownership table are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the credit agreement and indentures were not read, so restricted-payment capacity cannot be tested against the payouts.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 131
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better governance view is that family ownership aligns long-term incentives with a capital-intensive franchise, payouts are small beside capital spending, and no related-party leakage, restructuring or creditor-adverse transaction appears in the sources read, while customers are prepaying about USD 1.9 billion for capacity. The view would worsen on a debt-funded special distribution, related-party dealings disclosed in the proxy statement, a revolver draw to fund payouts, or loss of the largest customer's programs; it would improve if the proxy statement shows a majority of independent directors and no related-party payments and the debt documents show tight restricted-payment limits.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 131
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, related-party dealings and fee arrangements are not established; this keeps the Medium governance reading on incomplete evidence and could move it either way once read.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 131

- Contract terms and volumes by customer beyond the two named customers are not disclosed, so the customer concentration finding cannot be tied to contractual protection or to the durability of the largest customer's programs.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129

- The executed debt documents are not supplied, so restricted-payment and guarantee capacity are not established; the finding that payouts are small is relative to spending, not to what the debt agreements permit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

In May 2026 Amkor issued USD 1.15 billion of convertible senior notes due July 15, 2031 under an indenture dated May 5, 2026, including the full exercise of a USD 150 million option for additional notes. The notes carry a 0.00% coupon, are senior unsecured obligations guaranteed by Guardian Assets, Inc., cannot be redeemed before May 15, 2029 and are settled in cash up to principal with cash or shares for the excess. The conversion price is about USD 106.37 per share and none of the conditions for early conversion had been met at September 30, 2026. Alongside the issue Amkor bought capped calls for USD 56.4 million to reduce dilution; the notes' proceeds funded the capped calls and general corporate purposes including capital spending.

In 2025 Amkor replaced its bank and note funding: it entered a USD 1.0 billion senior secured revolving credit facility in May, added a USD 500.0 million term loan tranche in June, issued USD 500.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033 in September, and redeemed the remaining 2027 senior notes in July and October with the proceeds. A July 2026 Korean cash support agreement allows grants of up to about USD 110 million subject to performance conditions, of which about USD 11 million had been received.

The Board authorized a USD 300.0 million stock repurchase program on April 23, 2026, under which USD 32.3 million was bought in the third quarter; the regular quarterly dividend continues, with USD 62.1 million paid in nine months. In October 2026 Amkor agreed an advance payment arrangement with a customer under which it expects about USD 1.3 billion in 2027.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Amkor Technology, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the consolidated group's whole credit profile, from business model, ownership and cash conversion to liquidity, debt, downside and monitoring, drawn from the supplied filings through September 30, 2026 and the three earlier analyses.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-27 | 71c4688f61c8c8b537e875298c930c20e3abc00b6f57c61b7762a2695e5d6db0 | Latest statements and notes, debt, fair values, commitments, liquidity discussion, customer advances, covenant wording, capital returns, ownership and risk factors; the date is the signature page date. |

No external sources were used. Dates above are the signature page dates printed in each filing.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Amkor is a low-leverage, liquid credit entering a heavily debt-funded capacity build, so creditors are exposed to execution and customer-funding risk rather than to coverage or near-term maturities. Net leverage rose from 0.06x at the end of 2025 to 0.61x at September 30, 2026, or 0.64x pro forma for the Arizona land purchase expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, largely because nine-month capital spending of USD 1.24 billion exceeded operating cash flow of USD 868.35 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K01; calculation K03

Management guides to about USD 2.5 billion of capital spending in 2026, and customers are expected to prepay USD 1.9 billion within twelve months, but those advances are obligations to deliver capacity and have not been received. We read the credit as adequate today and weakening in direction.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; calculation K04
### Key findings

Debt service is not the constraint; the investment program is. Last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 1.41 billion covers accrued interest expense 19.30x, and in the first nine months of 2026 interest income of USD 59.12 million exceeded interest expense of USD 52.60 million, helped by the 0.00% coupon on the largest new issue, the convertible notes due 2031, and by interest capitalized on the Arizona build. Cash interest cover was 15.07x in FY2025 and cash interest for 2026 is not printed. The implication is that the debt stack could absorb a materially weaker earnings year before coverage became the issue, so the credit question is whether cash generation keeps pace with spending.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K02; calculation K23

Spending is committed ahead of the cash that will fund it, and the commitments grew faster than the guidance suggests. Contracted construction and development commitments rose from USD 475 million at the end of 2025 to USD 991 million at June 30, 2026 and USD 1,951 million at September 30, 2026, purchase obligations due within twelve months rose to USD 2,635.3 million from USD 1,084.8 million, and capital expenditure payables more than doubled to USD 496.13 million. Guidance for 2026 spending was USD 2.5 billion to USD 3.0 billion in the annual report and the June quarterly report and is now about USD 2.5 billion, which implies USD 1.26 billion in the fourth quarter against USD 548.38 million in the third; whether spending moved into 2027 is not stated. Net debt is therefore likely to keep rising into 2027 unless advances arrive on schedule.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 25, 36–37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_amkr_amkr-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 36–37; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78, 127; calculation K03; calculation K04; calculation K11; calculation K12

Customer advances now carry part of the build and part of the reported cash flow, so operating cash flow overstates what the business generates unaided. Contract liabilities rose by USD 156.8 million in the first nine months of 2026 and by USD 295.2 million in FY2025, together USD 452.0 million or 23.01% of operating cash flow over the 21 months, and 76.73% of the USD 547.6 million balance is recognized in revenue only after the next twelve months. Without the rise, nine-month operating cash flow would have been about USD 711.55 million and the free cash outflow about USD 525.26 million. Expected advances grew from about USD 300 million over two years at the end of 2025 to USD 1.9 billion within twelve months, of which only USD 200 million requires a standby letter of credit on receipt; the filings give no refund, delivery or cancellation terms, so how far advances behave like debt in a downside is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77, 103; calculation K07; calculation K08; calculation K09; calculation K10

The earnings base behind the build is improving but narrow. Third-quarter net sales were flat at USD 1,990.56 million, up 0.18%, while gross margin widened to 18.3% from 14.3% because materials cost fell USD 132.87 million on a lower-material-content mix, and conversion costs of labor, depreciation and other manufacturing rose USD 57.42 million, or 10.25%. Communications sales fell 28% on the timing of system-in-package transfers from Korea to Vietnam while computing and automotive and industrial each grew 37%. One customer was 29.8% and a second 11.1% of FY2025 net sales, the ten largest customers were 72%, and the filings give no contract terms. The margin gain is mix rather than price, and a few customers' program timing can move factory loading and earnings quickly.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 129; calculation K13; calculation K26

Liquidity and the maturity ladder are not the near-term risk. Cash and short-term investments of USD 2,376.2 million plus the undrawn USD 1,000 million revolver, which expires in May 2030, give USD 3,376.2 million against stated twelve-month obligations of USD 2,926.5 million, or 1.15x before operating cash flow and customer advances, although 57.09% of the cash and investments is held offshore and is reachable mainly by repaying intercompany debt. Only USD 348.89 million of principal falls due in 2027 to 2029 and 66.11% falls due after 2030, entirely the 2031 convertible and 2033 senior notes. Level 1 quotes put the 2033 senior notes at 94.77% of principal and the convertible at 90.71%, below par but not at distressed levels. The conversion price of the convertible is 2.23x the average price of the latest share repurchases and principal is settled in cash, so it is best read as cash debt due in 2031. Pro forma cash for the land purchase and the customer agreement is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 83; calculation K17; calculation K18; calculation K19; calculation K21

Financial policy is the main governance variable and is now being tested. Payouts of USD 94.43 million in nine months, made up of dividends of USD 62.10 million and repurchases of USD 32.33 million, continued while free cash flow was negative, and management states it aims to return 40% to 50% of cumulative free cash flow generated since 2022. Cumulative payouts are 45.08% of cumulative issuer-defined free cash flow, but a fourth-quarter free cash outflow above USD 105.71 million would lift that above 50% at current payouts, so either payouts slow, which supports creditors, or the framework is stretched. The Kim family holds 49.5% of the shares, so a sale or takeover is unlikely without family support and payout decisions rest with a family-influenced board; no related-party leakage is documented, but the proxy statement is not supplied and covenant levels are not printed, so room under the dividend restriction is not tested.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 74–76; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-K_2024-12-31_amkr_amkr-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 75, 88–89; calculation K22; calculation K28

Claims are layered in a way the consolidated figures do not show. Debt of USD 845.8 million is collateralized, an amount equal to the Term A Loans plus the Korean and Japanese subsidiary loans although the filing does not say which loans carry the collateral, the 2031 and 2033 notes are senior unsecured, and the parent's debt is structurally subordinated to all subsidiary liabilities. The undrawn secured revolver would rank ahead of the unsecured notes on pledged assets if it were drawn to fund the build, and the filings give no ranking or collateral by instrument for the subsidiary loans, so recovery for each class is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation K20
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a weakening view is that Amkor starts the build from low net leverage of 0.61x, or 0.64x pro forma for the expected land purchase, with net interest income, USD 3,376.2 million of cash, short-term investments and undrawn revolver, little principal due before 2030 and customers who are prepaying for capacity, which suggests the demand is contracted rather than hoped for. Capital spending that is not yet contracted can be deferred, and EBITDA margin moved up to 20.66% in the third quarter from 16.23% a year earlier. The case that the credit is weaker than that is that reported cash flow already leans on advances, commitments nearly doubled in one quarter, third-quarter sales barely grew, the largest customer is 29.8% of sales and covenants cannot be tested. The view would improve if advances arrive on schedule while 2027 spending is held back, if the USD 407 million government award starts to be received, or if quarterly free cash flow turns positive. It would worsen if advances slip, the revolver is drawn to fund spending, a major customer's programs are lost, the mix-driven margin gain reverses, or payouts continue after cumulative free cash flow falls below the level that supports them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–37; calculation K01; calculation K14; calculation K21; calculation K22
### Limitations

- The total cost of the Arizona facility and its spending after 2026 are not stated, so the conclusion that net debt keeps rising into 2027 rests on 2026 guidance and signed commitments, not on a full-program budget, and the size of the rise could be larger or smaller.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 25, 37

- Whether the advance figures overlap is not stated: the June report gave about USD 300 million over two years and a July agreement for about USD 1.5 billion in 2027, and the September report gives USD 1.9 billion within twelve months and an October agreement for about USD 1.3 billion in 2027, so the funding conclusion uses each figure separately and never adds them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_amkr_amkr-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is low leverage backed by large cash generation. Net leverage of 0.61x, 0.64x pro forma for the expected land purchase, and EBITDA cover of accrued interest of 19.30x mean a materially weaker earnings year would not by itself threaten debt service, which supports the ability to carry the build.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K01; calculation K23

The second strength is a back-ended maturity ladder and ample committed liquidity. Cash, short-term investments and the undrawn revolver exceed stated twelve-month obligations 1.15x, and 66.11% of principal falls due after 2030, so refinancing is not required before the build is complete.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation K19; calculation K21

The third strength is customer prepayment, which shows demand for the new capacity is backed by commitments from the customers that will use it, and which funds part of the spending without adding to debt. It is a strength only to the extent it is delivered, because the money is an obligation.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation K07; calculation K10

The fourth strength is a low cost of funding: the convertible notes carry a 0.00% coupon and interest income exceeded interest expense in nine months, so growth in gross debt has so far added little cash interest.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation K23

The first weakness is capital spending that exceeds operating cash flow. Spending of USD 1.24 billion against USD 868.35 million of operating cash flow in nine months, signed commitments of USD 1,951 million and guidance of about USD 2.5 billion mean net debt rises until the facility earns, and revenue from the first phase is not expected before the first half of 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 36–37; 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation K03; calculation K11

The second weakness is customer concentration with short commitments. One customer was 29.8% of FY2025 net sales, and the filings describe no backlog and short-term customer commitments, so a transfer or loss of programs moves utilization and margin before costs can be cut.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_amkr_amkr-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_amkr_amkr-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation K15

The third weakness is reliance on conditional and unreceived support: advances flatter operating cash flow, the USD 407 million government award has produced no cash and carries milestones and clawback rights, and the expected advances are partly unsecured by letters of credit.

The fourth weakness is limited visibility on creditor protections: payouts continue while free cash flow is negative, family control rests at 49.5%, covenant levels are not printed and the ranking of the subsidiary loans against the notes is not stated.

### Company description

Amkor is the largest US-headquartered outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider. It packages and tests chips designed by integrated device makers, fabless companies and foundries, usually on silicon wafers that the customer consigns, and reports one operating segment. The business model supports cash-flow visibility only in part: the filings describe short customer commitments and no backlog, so there is little contractual protection, but consigned wafers and customer responsibility for unused materials limit the inventory risk Amkor carries, and the move of sales toward computing and automotive reduces dependence on smartphones. The table that follows shows the mix and why it matters: the shift is real in the latest quarter, but one quarter's mix is also moved by the timing of program transfers.
